title: Welcome to Wimp Culture
summary: A scripted critique of Planet Fitness commercials as 'swole shaming': ads that mock fit people to flatter insecure customers. NH argues body positivity inverts values, keeps people weak so they keep paying, targets overweight women and weak men, and turns gyms into comfort zones instead of places of discomfort.
claims: Ten years ago slim and athletic people were common in public; now fat people are the norm among men in their 30s and women
If being fat is reframed as good, being strong and muscular becomes bad, which is why swole shaming is growing
Being uncomfortable around someone proud of their body means you feel worse about yourself; learn from them instead
Body positivity only allows pride in your body if you are not fit; achievement gets labeled arrogance
Letting weak people set values produces a morality that validates their shortcomings
The body-or-mind dichotomy contradicts the ancient ideal of developing body and soul together
Planet Fitness's swole-shaming marketing keeps customers small so they keep paying for a service that won't improve them
Gyms are supposed to be places of discomfort and adversity
The 'intimidating' hardcore gyms in the ads look better for making gains than sterile commercial gyms
Companies exploit women's beauty insecurities and then sell them excuses once they give up
Answer swole shaming with classic Apollonian virtue: respect beauty, treat sloth and envy as sins
